server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail as the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash, a draft is saved where another client can edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It archives and reports spam by role rather than by folder name, so on Gmail, with no archive folder, archiving drops the inbox label. It reads attachments: a PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. After a send, check_bounces says whether an address failed permanently or is still being retried, and check_receipts whether it was opened, even when the honest answer is that nothing came back. A diary connected as a separate step adds calendar tools: reading and searching events, free/busy, booking and moving your own time, inviting, cancelling, answering or proposing another time, and the out-of-office reply. A CardDAV address book connected to an IMAP mailbox, also separately, lets find_contact read the book beside the mailbox's own history, labelling each result's source, and adds read_contact to open one card. No contact is ever stored on the server. A mailbox with no diary or book is handed none of those tools rather than tools that refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar and contact tools are absent: each is registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary or an address book, and Outlook contacts on a Microsoft mailbox that reconnects, so listing them here would be a promise the server had not kept. find_contact is listed because every mailbox has it; a connected book improves it, and a writable one makes the contact tools five. The summary says what each adds.
